title: Do BBLs Stink? Causes, What's Normal and When to Call
meta_description: BBL smell comes from moisture, heat and an unwashed garment, not the surgery itself. What helps today and which signs mean call your surgeon.
excerpt: A plastic surgeon interviewed by ASPS says BBL smell is not a common or expected outcome. When odor happens, it usually comes from moisture, heat and friction under a garment. What's normal, what helps today and when a smell means you should call your surgeon.
quick_answer:
Do BBLs stink?

A plastic surgeon interviewed by ASPS says BBL smell is not a common or expected outcome with sterile surgery and proper aftercare. Odor usually comes from moisture, heat and friction under a garment. If it comes from an incision, or with redness, fever, more pain or a tender lump, call your surgeon.

What causes BBL smell

Most BBL odor comes from moisture:
Drainage from the liposuction incisions
A garment that traps heat and sweat
Hard-to-reach hygiene

Less often it is a sign of a complication:
Infection
An infected seroma
Fat necrosis, rarely

Sources: an ASPS article; The Aesthetic Society; Cleveland Clinic

Less likely urgent: smell comes from the garment or pads, improves after washing and showering, some leaking from liposuction incisions for several days, normal temperature. Call your surgeon: smell comes from one incision, gets stronger, thick cloudy white or cream discharge, redness spreading past the incision with warmth, fever above 101°F (38.4°C). Not sure? Call your surgeon. Infection signs usually appear 3–7 days after surgery, according to Cleveland Clinic.
